interim_updates.note_text: PickMe's parent, Digital Mobility Solutions Lanka, posted Rs.2.51bn revenue for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 40% YoY, with operating profit up 38% (Rs.602mn to Rs.833mn) and PAT up 45% (Rs.437mn to Rs.631mn), driven by a 40% YoY rise in average monthly unique consumers and a 64% rise in unique driver earners on the platform -- both reaching all-time highs. Gross Transaction Value (GTV, the total value of trips/deliveries facilitated, not statutory revenue) grew 48% YoY to Rs.25.3bn. Sequentially (QoQ, per the company's own commentary rather than a stored prior-quarter row), growth moderated from Q4 FY2025/26's seasonally strong result: total platform movements fell 2% QoQ and revenue was down 1% QoQ, as Middle East conflict-driven fuel rationing and rising fuel prices constrained driver availability and consumer affordability. Operating profit fell 15% QoQ (also citing higher IT infrastructure/subscription costs and currency depreciation) and PAT fell 10% QoQ from what the company describes as a 'record fourth-quarter result.'
interim_updates.gaps_note: No quarter ended 31 March 2026 (Q4 FY2025/26) report has been collected locally for PKME, so no structured QoQ row (qoq_json) can be built from stored financial_statements data -- the QoQ commentary above is transcribed from the company's own qualitative highlights section (p.2-3 of this filing), which states QoQ percentage changes without giving the absolute Q4 figures needed for a table. Revenue is a net platform-fee model with no cost-of-sales/gross-profit line, so those metrics are omitted entirely (not zero) from the YoY table above.
interim_updates.takeaway: YoY growth is broad-based and genuine (user base, driver base, and GTV all at record highs), but the QoQ softening -- entirely attributed by the company itself to fuel-supply disruption from the Middle East conflict and a seasonally strong Q4 comparison -- is worth watching next quarter to see if it's transient or the start of a trend.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.2.51bn, up 40% YoY; operating profit Rs.833mn (+38% YoY); PAT Rs.631mn (+45% YoY)
Average monthly unique consumers +40% YoY and unique driver earners +64% YoY, both at all-time highs on the platform
Gross Transaction Value (GTV, a non-SLFRS operational metric, not statutory revenue) grew 48% YoY to Rs.25.3bn
QoQ, per the company's own commentary: total platform movements -2%, revenue -1%, operating profit -15%, PAT -10% versus Q4 FY2025/26's seasonally strong 'record' quarter
Net cash used in investing activities Rs.1.19bn, mostly a Rs.966mn increase in other investments (up from Rs.14mn a year earlier) alongside continued capex on intangibles (Rs.204mn) and PPE (Rs.65mn)
key_drivers: YoY growth was driven by genuine platform expansion -- unique consumers +40%, unique driver earners +64%, both at record highs -- not a pricing or one-off effect

The company's own commentary attributes QoQ softening entirely to Middle East conflict-driven fuel rationing, which curbed driver availability, plus rising fuel prices weighing on consumer affordability and trip volumes

QoQ operating profit fell more than revenue (-15% vs -1%) because of higher IT infrastructure/subscription costs and currency depreciation on top of the softer volumes -- a margin, not just a volume, effect

PAT fell less than operating profit QoQ (-10% vs -15%), implying a partially offsetting improvement below the operating-profit line (net finance income or tax) that is not itemised in the company's narrative
